title: The Effect of Menstrual Pain on Cortical Networks and Postural Dynamics: A Combined EEG and Center-of-Pressure Study
summary: This cross-sectional study investigates whether balance control differs between healthy individuals with and without menstrual pain. Women with regular menstrual cycles will perform single-leg stance tasks on a stable and an unstable surface during menstruation. During the tasks, body sway and electrical brain activity will be recorded using electroencephalography (EEG). In addition, the intensity of menstrual pain and other potential influencing factors will be assessed. The aim of the study is to investigate whether women with and without menstrual pain differ in terms of body sway and brain connectivity during balance tasks.

interventions.name:
Participants with a regular and natural menstrual cycle perform single-leg stance tasks on stable and unstable surfaces on both their right and left legs during the early follicular phase (days 1–3 of the menstrual cycle).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Natural menstrual cycle (21-35 days with a maximum variation of 7 days)
Nulligravida
Group with menstrual pain: Score of 4 or higher on a visual numerical rating scale
Group without pain: No menstrual pain
Exclusion criteria:
No acute use of hormonal contraceptives or hormonal contraceptives use within the previous 9 months
No neurological, psychiatric, vestibular, neuromuscular or endocrinological diseases
No medication that could influence sex hormones
No acute injury of lower extremities or an injury within the previous 6 months
